facts.fact: 这次不一样——结束时 Soren 扯掉眼罩，那双黑眼睛锁住他的、不肯放开。
facts.anchor: This was… something else. And then right at the end, when he ripped the mask off just as he came, those dark eyes locked onto mine and refused to let go.

facts.fact: 本能狂喊让他转头躲开，他却留在原地没有移开视线。
facts.anchor: I couldn’t look away. Even when every instinct screamed at me to turn my head, to hide, to break the contact, I just… stayed there.

facts.fact: 这太越界了——不该发生在他与杀亲仇人之间。
facts.anchor: It felt far too intimate; like something that should never have happened between us. Between me and the man who killed my parents.

facts.fact: 他坚决对自己说：这没有任何意义，他就是喝醉了而已。
facts.anchor: It means nothing, I tell myself firmly. He’s drunk, that’s all, it doesn’t mean anything.

facts.fact: Soren 全身重量塌下来把他钉在床上，脸埋在他颈侧。
facts.anchor: My thoughts scatter when his full weight suddenly collapses on top of me. Soren is so much bigger than I am. The air leaves my lungs in a sharp huff as I’m pinned beneath all that solid muscle and heat.

facts.fact: 醉话命令：明天你上桌吃早餐。
facts.anchor: You’ll… have breakfast at the table tomorrow.

facts.fact: 他困惑：从没被允许上过桌，之前都是厨房跟 Lorraine 吃或带回房间。
facts.anchor: He’s never wanted me at the table before. I’m usually allowed to eat in the kitchen with Lorraine or just take something back to my room. Why would he suddenly want me sitting there with the rest of them?

facts.fact: 荒唐的恐慌念头：万一就这样卡住了怎么办？万一弄不出来怎么办？
facts.anchor: A ridiculous, panicked thought flashes through my head… what if we actually get stuck like this? What if I can’t get him out?

facts.fact: 通常都是 Soren 动手动脚——今晚轮到他必须勇敢。
facts.anchor: Usually, it’s Soren doing all the touching. Tonight I have to be brave.

facts.fact: 他小心抬起那只沉重的手，把粗壮的手臂抬高一点钻出来，再轻轻放回床垫。
facts.anchor: I carefully pick up his heavy hand, lift his thick arm just high enough to slide out from under it, and lower it back onto the mattress as gently as I can.

facts.fact: 屏住呼吸推门缝挤出去，再用发酸的慢动作把门合上不让锁舌咔哒。
facts.anchor: I ease one door open just wide enough to slip through, holding my breath the entire time, and pull it shut behind me with aching slowness so the latch doesn’t click.

facts.fact: 走廊全黑全空，寂静比噪音更沉；手腕还捆着——先回房间。
facts.anchor: The hallway is completely dark and empty; no voices, no footsteps, nothing. The silence feels heavier than noise ever could. It presses in from both ends of the long corridor, making the back of my neck prickle. I glance left, then right, heart still hammering, and then I’m turning toward the back staircase as fast as I can without actually running. I still have to figure out a way to get my wrists free, but first, I need my room.
